message.content: Confirmed the fuzzer's energy violation — now triaging to isolate the cause.
Shrunk the failure to a minimal two-body case — now inspecting the collision sequence to pinpoint the energy blowup.
The numbers show a single high-speed impact quadrupling total energy — now testing what triggers it.

function.arguments: {"scenario_id":"sb2f24787ce","rule":"energy_bound","explanation":"Shrunk scenario shows deterministic energy explosion at the first body-body collision. At step 8 energy is ~3125 J (below E0=3316 J) and bodies are separated. At step 9 bodies are touching (gap 0.047) after 42 substeps and total energy jumps to 14969 J (~4.5x), far above allowed 3652 J, with controller disabled (work 0). High restitution (e=0.9 and 1.0) combined with high relative speed (~60 m/s closing) makes the impulse/positional-correction add kinetic energy instead of conserving/dissipating it. Counterfactual with e=0 for both bodies keeps energy at ~2312 J and removes the violation.","citations":[{"body":-1,"claim":"energy just before collision is below initial, no violation","field":"energy","step":8,"value":3125.491896317114},{"body":-1,"claim":"first energy_bound violation — energy ~4.5x initial, exceeds 3652 allowed","field":"energy","step":9,"value":14969.333903204535},{"body":1,"claim":"body 1 speed more than doubles across the colliding step, showing spurious kinetic gain","field":"speed","step":8,"value":22.80038834935362},{"body":1,"claim":"body 1 speed after collision","field":"speed","step":9,"value":64.34905860934973}],"counterfactual":{"scenario_id":"sb604318586","change":"Set restitution e=0 for both bodies (was 0.9 and 1.0). With perfectly inelastic collision the spurious energy gain disappears and energy stays below initial (2312 J < 3316 J), so energy_bound no longer violated. Proves high-e restitution handling in the collision impulse is the cause."}}
